solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Like upcycled furniture rescued from skip?

definitions.meaning: old chairs given a fresh layer of fabric have been ...
something saved from a builder's rubbish container has been salvaged or got back

explanation.surface: A thrift-minded hobbyist describes a chair saved from a builder's rubbish container and given new fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: A skip is the British name for a large open rubbish container on a building site. The same letters read as re-covered (new upholstery) and as salvaged.
explanation.definitionFit: Furniture with new upholstery has literally been covered again, while anything salvaged from a rubbish container has been got back.

clue.text: Hear strange bird

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of the word before it are in an odd, altered order

explanation.surface: Someone hears an unfamiliar birdcall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges HEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless South American ratite, related to the ostrich and emu.

clue.text: Noisy revelling — endless feature of funfair

indicators.note: endless says the word for the funfair ride loses its final letter

parts.note: a carousel, the merry-go-round, is a typical attraction at a fair

explanation.surface: Loud partying, a never-ending part of the fairground experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the last letter L from CAROUSEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A carouse is a noisy drinking party or bout of boisterous merrymaking.

clue.text: Tax vessel

definitions.meaning: value added tax, the British sales levy, is known by its initials
a large tank or container for liquids, as in brewing

explanation.walkthrough: VAT is value added tax, the British equivalent of a sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation for a consumption levy is also an ordinary word for a big storage tank.

clue.text: Engineers crazy — bridge finally constructed anew

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
crazy means mad

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word bridge

explanation.surface: Mad engineers have rebuilt a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers; 'finally' takes E, the end of 'bridge'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rebuilt has been fashioned again from scratch, which is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Hide crack somehow in seat outdoors

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some unspecified new way

explanation.surface: Instructions to conceal a split in a garden seat.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram indicator rearranges the letters of HIDE CRACK.
explanation.definitionFit: A folding canvas chair is the classic seat used on a beach or a lawn.

clue.text: Rod reported character at start of quarrel

indicators.note: reported means the letter is to be heard as spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: the opening character of the word quarrel is the letter Q

explanation.surface: Someone reports a rod as the first point of contention in a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter Q, said aloud, sounds like the snooker rod.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker and billiards the tapered stick used to strike the ball is called this.

clue.text: Gracious! US private gets dog!

parts.note: Cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like Gracious!
a GI is an American enlisted soldier

explanation.surface: Astonishment that an American soldier has acquired a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is a British exclamation of surprise; GI is an American soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh corgi is a short-legged breed, famously favoured by Queen Elizabeth II.

clue.text: English bird on a lake, timeless

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: An English seabird on a lake makes a timeless scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Something everlasting is outside time, never beginning or ending.

clue.text: Maturer when going wrong, making mistake

indicators.note: going wrong suggests the letters of the word before it have been jumbled

explanation.surface: An older person slips up when things go awry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going wrong' rearranges MATURER.
explanation.definitionFit: An erratum is an error in print, especially one listed in a correction slip; Latin for a thing gone astray.

clue.text: Swear, the way things go without love

indicators.note: without tells us to leave out the letter for love from the word before

parts.note: the course of events is the way things proceed
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone swears at how life is turning out when love is absent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes O (love, nil in tennis) from COURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter oaths or profanities is to use bad language, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Legal power? Judge is enthralling old city with speech

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the city is held within the first two pieces

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
diction is the manner of speaking

explanation.surface: A judge captivating an ancient city with an oration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enthralling' signals the insertion. Ur, in ancient Mesopotamia, is the crossword's favourite old city; the question mark flags a definition by description.
explanation.definitionFit: Jurisdiction is the authority a court or official has to hear cases and make rulings.

clue.text: Question Milan team outlook

parts.note: Inter Milan is one of the city's two big football clubs
an outlook is a view

explanation.surface: Pondering the prospects of a Milanese football club.
explanation.walkthrough: Inter Milan is a famous Italian football club.
explanation.definitionFit: To interview someone is to put questions to them, as a verb; the swap works.

clue.text: Quite nice

definitions.meaning: an adverb meaning fairly or rather
an adjective meaning attractive or pleasing to look at

explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb the word means fairly or rather; as an adjective it means attractive or appealing.

clue.text: Chatter about old boy getting certificate

indicators.note: about means going round, so the chatter surrounds the old boy

parts.note: to prate is to chatter on foolishly
OB is a standard abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: Gossip surrounding a former pupil who has received a document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the insertion; an old boy is a former pupil of a British school.
explanation.definitionFit: Probate is the official document confirming a will is valid and the executor may act.

clue.text: Package in unusual place outside front of restaurant

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged letters go around the next piece
unusual suggests the letters of the word place are arranged in an uncommon way
front of picks the leading letter of restaurant

explanation.surface: A package turns up in an odd spot just outside a restaurant's entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges PLACE to PACEL; 'outside' puts it around R, the 'front of restaurant'.
explanation.definitionFit: A parcel is a wrapped package, especially one sent by post.

clue.text: Firm up arrangement for tenant in two lines of text

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a let is a rental agreement for a property

explanation.surface: Formalising a rental agreement written in two lines.
explanation.walkthrough: A let is the British term for a rental of a property.
explanation.definitionFit: A couplet is a pair of consecutive rhyming lines of verse.

clue.text: Web-user starts to see problem, idea not quite right

indicators.note: starts to takes the opening letter of each of the next two words
not quite means the word idea loses its last letter

explanation.surface: An internet user starts to spot a problem with a nearly correct idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' gives S and P; 'not quite' trims IDEA to IDE. 'Web-user' looks like an internet surfer.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider spins and uses a silk web to catch prey, a witty description.

clue.text: Rowdy Robert in trouble with spouse

indicators.note: in trouble suggests both names are thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: A noisy man called Robert falls out with his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' rearranges ROBERT and SPOUSE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstreperous means noisy and hard to control, a direct synonym of unruly.

clue.text: Corporal punishment to stay

definitions.meaning: a beating with a cane, as in getting the cane
to remain fixed in place, to adhere

explanation.surface: Corporal punishment is here to stay.
explanation.definitionFit: Harsh treatment or a beating is informally called this, and the verb also means to remain or adhere.

clue.text: Conservative cheated country

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative, the British political party
to be had is to be tricked or cheated

explanation.surface: A Tory politician swindled the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had' in the sense of 'conned', as in 'you've been had'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chad is a landlocked nation in north-central Africa.

clue.text: Old-style politician involved in excellent excuse

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped inside, so the politician sits within the other piece

parts.note: A1 means first-rate; the figure 1 serves as the letter I
Lib is short for a Liberal, a party now merged into the Liberal Democrats

explanation.surface: A traditional politician caught up in a superb pretext.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' places LIB inside A1, with the numeral 1 read as I. The old Liberal party merged in 1988.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere, and loosely any excuse.

clue.text: Temptress greeted on return outside Lima

indicators.note: outside means those letters go around the Lima letter
on return means the word for greeted is read backwards

parts.note: to hail is to greet, so greeted gives hailed
Lima is L in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A seductress is welcomed back to the Peruvian capital's outskirts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on return' turns HAILED into DELIAH; 'outside' puts that around L. Lima suggests Peru but is the radio code for L.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible Delilah seduced Samson and betrayed him, making her the archetypal seductress.

clue.text: Meadow bare, having been cut

indicators.note: having been cut means the word has lost its last letter

parts.note: lean means meagre or bare, as in lean times

explanation.surface: A grassy field stripped after mowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having been cut' drops N from LEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lea is a poetic word for a grassy field or pasture.

clue.text: Animal in shackles falling back

indicators.note: falling back means those letters are read in reverse
in says the letters are sitting within the word shackles

explanation.surface: A beast in chains retreats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds KLE in 'shackles'; 'falling back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The elk is a large deer, the moose in North America.

clue.text: Justified state of conflict and spoke angrily

parts.note: war is a state of armed conflict
to rant is to speak loudly and angrily

explanation.surface: Someone argues that hostility was fair and shouted about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something called for or merited by circumstances is justified.
